elements_not_encoded.text: Give emergency contraception if patient had unprotected sex in past 5 days and does not want pregnancy:
elements_not_encoded.reason: Red-box header is the indication for giving emergency contraception (a medicine). It is not an urgent-attention box and the page assigns no priority; encoding it as a priority or diagnosis would add logic the page does not state. No manage tasks in this pass.

elements_not_encoded.text: Check pregnancy test and if negative, insert Copper IUD1 as soon as possible or give single dose levonorgestrel 1.5mg orally.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Pregnancy test then Copper IUD or levonorgestrel 1.5mg: management (lab test, device, medicine dose).

elements_not_encoded.text: If patient > 80kg, BMI2 ≥ 30, or on efavirenz, rifampicin, phenytoin or carbamazepine, offer Copper IUD1 or increase dose of levonorgestrel to 3mg.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Dose/method adjustment for weight > 80kg, BMI >= 30 or enzyme-inducing drugs: medicine choice and dose.

elements_not_encoded.text: If patient on ketoconazole/fluconazole, advise levonorgestrel may cause nausea/vomiting and offer Copper IUD1 instead.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Method choice and advice for patients on ketoconazole/fluconazole: management.

elements_not_encoded.text: If patient vomits < 2 hours after taking levonorgestrel, repeat dose.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Repeat levonorgestrel dose if vomited within 2 hours: medicine dosing.

elements_not_encoded.text: Offer to start long-term contraceptive at same visit (if IUD not chosen). If injectable or implant given, check pregnancy test in 2 weeks.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Start long-term contraceptive and follow-up pregnancy test in 2 weeks: management/follow-up.

elements_not_encoded.text: Assess for HIV and hepatitis B post-exposure prophylaxis 119. Advise patient to return for pregnancy test if next period is more than 7 days late.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Assess for HIV/hepatitis B PEP (pointer to 119) and advice to return for pregnancy test: management and cross-reference.

judgment_calls.topic: Red box encoded as management only
judgment_calls.decision: All 7 red-box elements are management_step; no check_for task or priority evaluation is built from the emergency-contraception box.
judgment_calls.alternatives: A check_for task triggered by unprotected sex checking 'does not want pregnancy', or an Urgent priority for unprotected sex within 5 days. Rejected: the page gives no priority and no diagnosis, and those findings would be checked for but never used as evidence.

judgment_calls.topic: Scope of 'when using combined oral contraceptive'
judgment_calls.decision: Applied to all three signs (nausea, breast tenderness, missed period), as the parenthesis reads.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Apply only to missed period, letting nausea or breast tenderness alone suggest pregnancy in any contraception user; would fire more often.

judgment_calls.decision: 'Check for symptoms of STIs: vaginal discharge, ulcers, lower abdominal pain. If present 62' treated as a routing pointer to page 62, not as a 'consider STI' rule.
judgment_calls.alternatives: A possible STI diagnosis from any of the three symptoms; rejected because the page does not say 'consider/suspect' and page 62 owns that logic.

judgment_calls.decision: BP >= 140/90 (148), BMI >= 25 (156), breast/axilla lumps (55/42), menopause (187), HIV (124/126/119), cervical screen (70), suitability (172), missed pills (171) are cross-references or management; not encoded. BP, weight and height are routine vitals so no measure task.
judgment_calls.alternatives: check_for tasks for breast lumps or menopausal symptoms; would leave findings unused on this page.
